articles.body: “No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta, one of many organised across the US on Saturday. While many demonstrators denounced President Donald Trump’s policies, organisers said the rally was aimed at getting out the vote in the November 3 midterm elections and protecting democracy in America.
articles.headline: ‘Standing up for democracy’: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally draws Trump critics ahead of midterms

articles.body: Looters on Saturday seized the opportunity to raid and vandalise a host of shops and businesses across France – from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores – as hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets to protest higher living costs and other grievances.
articles.headline: Looters seize on massive French protests to raid and vandalise shops

articles.body: In Brazil, deforestation in the Amazon has reached its lowest level in 40 years. President Lula is bolstering his environmental record just over a week before the second round of the presidential election, in which he faces Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.headline: Brazil: Amazon deforestation at 40-year low

articles.body: "Mothers of Kherson" has opened at Poland's National Opera. The performance was co-produced with New York's Metropolitan Opera and created in close association with Save Ukraine, a group helping to bring back Ukrainian children who remain in Russia. More than four years after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the opera aims to "reawaken" global interest in the war.
articles.headline: Ukraine war: "Mothers of Kherson" opera opens in Poland

articles.body: Police and protesters clashed in Paris and other French cities on Saturday, with smoke from fires and tear gas filling the air at demonstrations nationwide against high prices, ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. "Two fires broke out in Place de la République," reports France 24's Antonia Kerrigan from the ground.
articles.headline: Protests in France: "Two fires broke out in Place de la République"

articles.body: The teenage gunman who shot dead three children and a teacher in an Oregon school was a former special needs student there, officials said Friday, as they praised the heroism of people who helped to shorten the rampage.
articles.headline: US: Four killed in Oregon school shooting

articles.body: Saturday’s mobilisation in France follows calls on social media to revive the Yellow Vests movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Student groups protesting since mid-September have urged supporters to join. We discuss this with our journalist on the ground, Antonia Kerrigan, and our guest, Paul Smith, head of Modern Languages at the University of Nottingham.
articles.headline: Protests in France: "Living conditions are too harsh"

articles.body: In France, protests are under way across the country this Saturday. Demonstrators are protesting against the high cost of living, as well as poor working and studying conditions. We discuss this with France 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet.
articles.headline: France: What's different about today's protests?

articles.body: Protesters across France called for street demonstrations on Saturday against rising living costs. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from Paris. "The march from here to Place de Clichy isn't set to start for another hour. However, we've seen it kicking off extremely early doors. It seems that what's happened is that police attempted to block the protesters from reaching Place de la République, and we saw the use of tear gas. We've seen people running with their masks on. We also saw the use of stun grenades."
articles.headline: France: "We've seen extremely high tensions between protesters and law enforcement"

articles.body: 190 000 people could demonstrate this Saturday in France. They called for street demonstrations Saturday against rising living costs, joining high school students' grievances over education conditions after more than three weeks of school blockades.
articles.headline: France: Students, unions and Yellow Vests unite against austerity

articles.body: Skydance’s $110 billion creation tests whether France’s cultural exception can still compel a leveraged global media giant to fund, protect and prioritise French creativity, or merely treat it as a compliance cost.
articles.headline: Will Paramount’s creation of Skydance test France’s cultural exception?

articles.body: Protesters clashed with police in Paris and other French cities on Saturday as hundreds of thousands took to the streets to protest higher living costs and the declining conditions in schools and other public services. Several town halls were broken into – and in at least one instance set on fire – and many shops were vandalised and ransacked. One protester had his hand torn off by what appeared to be a crowd-control grenade used by police.
articles.headline: Fires and clashes rock France amid massive nationwide protests

articles.body: French authorities detained dozens on Saturday at the start of nationwide protests against the cost of living, in what is likely to be a key indicator of the social climate heading toward elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.
articles.headline: France faces day of cost-of-living protests

articles.body: Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in the north-western city of Bamenda. A young woman was also killed as the attackers opened fire on mourners attending a wake. The shooting has renewed concerns about the dangers facing journalists in Cameroon's English-speaking regions, after years of conflict between government forces and separatist groups.
articles.headline: Cameroonian journalist shot in Bamenda

articles.body: The town of Masaka in southern Uganda is currently conducting a Phase 1 trial of a vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which is circulating in the region. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for this strain.
articles.headline: Uganda launches Ebola vaccine trial

articles.body: Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The health ministry said the 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine, where she has been since 5 October. The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, is in a stable condition. Health officials say there is no evidence of community transmission, as both individuals were under quarantine. However, three contacts have yet to be traced. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
articles.headline: Kenya reports third Ebola case, contact tracing continues

articles.body: GIRDWOOD, Alaska — Dan Sullivan isn’t running away from President Donald Trump like so many other vulnerable Republicans. He’s betting that walking the line instead will help him reap reelection in November. During a candidate debate, speaking at an economic forum and in an interview with Playbook this week, Sullivan repeatedly denied chances to put distance between himself and Trump’s most unpopular policies and positions. Has the economic pain from the war with Iran been worth it for Alaskans? “The real economic pain is when Democrats get control,” Sullivan told POLITICO, sitting in the shadow of a well-antlered taxidermy moose head, next to a roaring fire, at a ski resort tucked up in the mountains off the Turnagain Arm southeast of Anchorage. What about the $5,000 dividends Trump has promised voters if Republicans hold control of Congress, as he did at a rally for Sullivan in Wasilla on Tuesday? “I’ve got to look at the legislation. I don't know,” Sullivan said. “That was the first time I heard it from him, and I would just evaluate that if and when it happens.” Does he want to see data centers — which Trump has pushed for further development despite some pushback from local communities — pop up on Alaska’s undeveloped land? He’s not putting his foot down. “They definitely got to pay their own way in terms of energy,” Sullivan said. “They have to have local input and approval, and we’ll see.” Still, Sullivan bristled on some issues that touch closer to home. In light of Trump’s decision to import Russian diesel, did Sullivan think the Trump administration was being too friendly with Russia? “I thought you were asking me campaign stuff,” Sullivan replied. “Is this like a hit piece or what?” “I know my view on Russia. I'm very hawkish on Russia,” Sullivan continued, pointing to an op-ed he wrote during Trump's first administration about whether the president was too close with Russian President Vladimir Putin. “I wrote an op-ed essentially saying, sometimes I don't agree with the rhetoric, but at the end of the day, what does Putin understand? He understands power. What's the ultimate source of power that the Russians fear? U.S. military power, which Republicans always build up, Democrats always cut.” Though his office put out a statement decrying the diesel move, Sullivan didn’t sign a bipartisan letter calling on the president to reverse the decision — which he said he never saw — and instead took his concerns straight to the White House. “I speak to the administration all the time on the issues of high energy costs,” Sullivan said. Art Hackney, a veteran Republican strategist in Alaska who runs a pro-Sullivan super PAC called “We Stand with Dan,” said in an interview that another part of the calculus is that Murkowski has provided a straightforward example of how Trump treats Republicans who publicly disagree with him. “If Dan did something considered a disrespectful trigger or something, what do you think would happen? It could well have implications for things that affect Alaska's economy.” But Trump, for better or worse, is a centerpiece of races like Sullivan’s. The president has pleaded with voters at rallies to “pretend I'm on the ballot” — just as he did alongside Sullivan on Tuesday. And Alaska’s tighter-than-expected Senate race is poised to be a linchpin for deciding which party holds control of the chamber. Alaska, Ohio and Iowa are the races that Trump officials view as increasingly critical to keep their majority, according to three GOP officials familiar with the Trump-aligned super PAC MAGA Inc.’s strategy, granted anonymity to candidly assess the midterms. Sullivan only sees Trump’s presence as a boon. “I think the rally certainly helps in terms of energizing the base,” Sullivan said. He’s proud to have the president campaign alongside him, plus Vice President JD Vance, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas). “I'm bringing up my people,” Sullivan said. “I’m not afraid of that.” Polls show Sullivan tied with or trailing former Rep. Mary Peltola, one of Democrats’ top hopes to help flip the Senate. On paper, this contest shouldn’t be close: Peltola lost her House seat after just one term. “It was Trump plus-13 two years ago, so it is not the position we’d love to be in, but we’re doing what we do to help get him across the finish line,” said Kevin Greene, the state director for Americans for Prosperity-Alaska, which has knocked on tens of thousands of doors for Sullivan. On one such door-to-door trip with Greene in Anchorage on Thursday morning, voters across approximately a dozen houses were about evenly split between supporting Sullivan or Peltola. Only one agreed to speak on the record to POLITICO: John Baker, a 67-year-old retiree who said he used to be a Republican but would be supporting Peltola this year. What happened? “Donald Trump happened,” Baker said. He added that his support for Peltola was 70% because he wanted to see Democrats take the Senate and 30% because he liked her as a candidate. Peltola, the first Alaska Native to represent the state in Congress, has centered her campaign around “fish, family, and freedom” while capitalizing on voters’ frustrations with the high cost of energy and goods, particularly in remote communities. She has focused on outreach to villages in the Alaskan bush and has largely shied away from national attention, including from the media. The former congresswoman has some major liabilities that Sullivan often slams. Just two years ago, she lost her reelection bid after only one full term. She has sought to distance herself from the Biden administration, which remains unpopular in the state. She has a reputation for missing meetings and votes. And a New York Times report last month alleged that she created a hostile work environment and regularly used slurs and other offensive language. Even those close to her campaign, though optimistic, acknowledge it’s still an uphill battle. “It’s always been long odds,” said John-Henry Heckendorn, a Democratic strategist in Alaska whose firm is supporting Peltola outside of her official campaign. Peltola, he said, would have to do about twice as well as the Democratic Senate challengers in the past four cycles in order to win. At the debate on Thursday, Peltola said she “prided” herself on being “available to Alaskan press” — though she acknowledged she has “really demurred from national attention, from national outlets.” After the debate, POLITICO asked Peltola: “You said you’re accessible to the press. Will you take some questions?” She smiled, then walked away quickly, with an aide saying she had a dinner to attend. “She’s hoping that the Joe Biden bunker mentality will win, and you know, maybe it will,” Sullivan told POLITICO on Friday. “I don't think it will. I think Alaskans can see through it.” Peltola’s campaign declined several interview requests for this story. In an email to POLITICO, the campaign noted that Sullivan was in the top quarter of most-absent senators , and that Peltola had to miss congressional votes when both her husband and mother died. The email also noted that Peltola helped secure the Willow oil-drilling project and has a record of bucking her fellow Democrats. Peltola has hosted at least 16 events in Alaska this month, the campaign said, and has interviewed with eight news outlets in the past week. “Dan Sullivan has tripled his wealth in the Senate and voted fourteen times for the war in Iran that is raising costs one everything from gas to groceries, Mary has been talking with Alaskans in every corner of the state about her plan to take on the rigged system in DC, lower costs, and put Alaska first,” Harry Child, a campaign spokesperson, said in a statement to POLITICO. Sullivan is leaning on his strong legislative record and support for oil and gas development in the state. He has sought to tie Peltola to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, and has attributed her massive fundraising edge to “lower-48 liberal millionaires and billionaires who want to turn Alaska into national parks.” Though he’s largely embracing Trump, there’s still moments of disagreement. But even in those spaces, he’s touting his close ties to the White House and effectiveness as a Washington operator instead of pushing the president away. Sullivan was opposed to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream the execution of the convicted Fort Hood shooter, and told POLITICO “there’s probably no senator weighing in more with senior White House and directly with the Secretary of War than me, saying this is not a good idea.” Trump called off the livestream on Thursday . Trump’s approval rating here, like the country at large, is underwater. The war with Iran has hit Alaska hard, where nearly all goods are imported by plane or barge, with urban gas prices hovering around $5 per gallon and prices in the bush often double that. In a year when Republican voters may be more likely to stay home without Trump on the ballot — Democrats eye an opening. “We have a golden opportunity with a fantastic candidate on our end and a really mediocre one on theirs,” said Alaska Democratic Party Chair Eric Croft. “I think we've been coming that way for a long time, and this is our chance to pump through.” Trump on Tuesday flew more than eight hours from Washington to Wasilla, home of Sarah Palin and the Iditarod, with Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, FCC Chair Brendan Carr and FHFA Administrator Bill Pulte in tow. He announced that Taiwan had joined South Korea in its commitments to a proposed Alaska energy pipeline — though the project is still in flux — and that the FCC will vote this month to invest an additional $162 million to expand high-speed internet in the state. Thousands of the president’s fans piled into the ice hockey rink and thousands more gathered outside, watching Trump speak on a jumbotron. Asked by POLITICO what he thought about Peltola, rally attendee Jeff Caswell, 59, replied: “I don’t.” But in a state where independents outnumber Republicans, that enthusiasm may only go so far. “Very conservative MAGA voters can’t vote for you harder,” said Scott Kendall, a veteran political strategist who worked on two of Alaska GOP Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s campaigns and was chief of staff to former Alaska Gov. Bill Walker. “Donald Trump’s support in this current climate is both a blessing and a curse,” Kendall noted. Even some reliable Trump supporters at the rally acknowledged the outlook appeared bleak. “I think Alaska’s turning blue,” Matt Niessink, a 45-year-old general contractor from Wasilla, said at the rally. He said he had voted for Trump three times and planned to support Republicans this year. What did he wish the president would do differently? “I wish he’d shut his mouth sometimes and not be such a pompous ass,” Niessink said.
articles.headline: ‘Is this like a hit piece or what?': Dan Sullivan's MAGA balancing act

articles.body: Donald Trump is barnstorming the country to boost Republicans in the final weeks of the midterms. But many candidates want to keep that support quiet. The president is nowhere to be found in GOP ads, even in red states where Republicans were happy to tout his endorsement two years ago. And some candidates are hesitant to appear with Trump on the campaign trail — even as they hope he will help juice turnout among the MAGA base in November. Democratic House and Senate candidates and outside groups have spent $145 million on general election ads mentioning Trump, while Republicans have spent just $8 million, according to a POLITICO analysis of data from AdImpact, which tracks political advertising. That’s in sharp contrast to 2024, when GOP candidates spent $62 million on ads mentioning Trump. “Trump is at historic lows right now, so if he comes to your district or state, it’s about getting the Republican base vote out there and that can certainly help,” said Ron Bonjean, a longtime GOP strategist. “But it's really important for the candidates not to be talking about Trump 24/7 on the campaign trail.” The unfavorable national political environment leaves few incentives for GOP candidates to tie themselves to Trump, and more and more Republicans in competitive races have broken with the president on issues such as the Iran war and tariffs. When Republicans do mention Trump in ads, they often aren’t touting his support. In Alaska, GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan has run an ad citing how he “voted to force Trump's DOJ to release the Epstein files.” The silence on the airwaves is especially stark in red states like Nebraska and Ohio. In 2024, Sen. Deb Fischer (R-Neb.), who was facing a challenge from independent Dan Osborn, and now-Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), who was challenging then-Sen. Sherrod Brown, both ran several general election ads featuring endorsements from Trump. The president won Nebraska by more than 20 points and Ohio by 12 points that year, with Fischer and Moreno also winning their races. But this cycle, the GOP isn’t focusing its ads on Trump in either state, as the match-up between Osborn and Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts heats up in Nebraska and Brown seeks to oust Republican Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio. Both Ricketts and Husted appeared at Trump rallies earlier this month. Still, Trump is absent from all Republican Senate ads in Ohio, and the only Ricketts ads that name the president accuse Osborn of disparaging Trump supporters — but don’t mention Trump’s endorsement. "The war in Iran, I think, has become a real noose around the neck of Republican candidates because of the affordability crisis," said former Ohio Rep. Jim Renacci. A nonprofit he works with surveyed voters on whether GOP candidates should appear with Trump and found that "in most cases you do not want [Trump] standing near you, which is why I was a little bit surprised that Jon Husted has had two events with President Trump, because I do believe there's a strong headwind in Ohio, and a big change from 2024." Husted’s campaign spokesperson Amy Natoce told POLITICO in a statement, “President Trump won Ohio decisively three times by 8 points, 8 points and 11 points. If we successfully turn out the MAGA vote this November, then we will retire Sherrod Brown for good.” The National Republican Senatorial Committee did not respond to a request for comment. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said. “The choice has never been more clear: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ extreme liberal policies and obstruction.” Another Republican operative, who is based in Ohio and like others was granted anonymity to speak candidly about their own party, said GOP candidates need to find a way to talk about the Trump administration — no tax on tips, protecting social security — without mentioning the guy in the Oval Office. “This is a historically unpopular president,” said the strategist, who has worked on multiple statewide races over the course of the last 15 years. “We all agree with that, and so it's kind of hard to attach yourself on the airways, I think, too closely to him.” Trump’s rallies, unlike candidates’ ads, are seen more as targeting the president’s base. He’s not only visiting traditional battlegrounds like Georgia and Michigan, but also typically safe red states like Alabama and Kansas. Still, his events have been a source of tension with some GOP candidates. When Trump’s team was making plans for the president to campaign in Michigan last week potentially in western Michigan, several Republican candidates and their teams up and down the ticket initially didn't know whether they should attend and be seen with the president, according to three Republicans with direct knowledge of the conversations, who were granted anonymity to share private details. They were concerned about being associated with Trump’s tariffs, which have hammered the state, along with high fuel prices amid the Iran war. Trump officials scrapped the event and said the president would visit the state later in the month. Trump is now scheduled for a rally in the state on Oct. 25. "[Republican candidates] are going to do what they need to do," said one GOP pollster close to the White House. "What the White House and the president are doing is they are targeting places where they think the president can be helpful.” Trump has allowed Republicans to discuss issues pertaining to their states or districts as “he understands that it is not a balk on him,” said one White House official, granted anonymity to speak candidly. If Trump “was to believe that all these individuals were balking him, I A) don’t think that he would want to be on the road every day, and B) I do think that you would probably see a more vocal President Donald J. Trump on Truth, et cetera, kind of voicing his opinion on it,” the official said. The president and his team are giving most Senate GOP candidates especially a wide latitude to break with some of his policies at times, according to two other White House officials involved in the conversations. Trump, they said, understands the need for vulnerable candidates to create some distance, even though in the past he has lashed out at members of his party for similar moves. Republicans in the more MAGA-friendly House, however, are expected to run more in lock-step with the president. Only the most at-risk candidates are afforded some room to break with Trump, the officials said, given the tidal wave of chaos that can spur within the conference. One GOP strategist working on a battleground House race, granted anonymity to discuss private information, said he had gotten pre-approved from the White House for his candidate to miss a planned rally. Still, the strategist cautioned, that doesn't mean Trump won't berate someone from the stage when he notices the candidate is missing. Republicans still see Trump as a unique motivator for his base and rallies as a tool to help turn out voters who might be driven by the president. With Democratic voters already energized by opposing Trump, the GOP has less to lose by bringing the president out to turn out MAGA voters too. “The reality is, Democrats are going to vote in this midterm,” said Paul Shumaker, a Republican strategist from North Carolina, where Trump is set to return for a rally next week as GOP Senate nominee Michael Whatley struggles to close the gap in his race. “And what Republicans need to be doing is focus on what they can do to improve their voter turnout on their side.” Lauren Fedor, Myah Ward, Andrew Howard and Alex Gangitano contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Not all Republicans want to show Trump off

articles.body: WICHITA, Kansas — Roger Marshall was running behind. The bus Kansas Republicans booked for a five-day barnstorming tour sat idling Tuesday morning, with other statewide candidates onboard. The tour was already a few minutes delayed as state party chair Danedri Herbert awaited word from the senator who some Republicans grumble isn’t campaigning hard enough as polls show him tied or trailing . Finally, she got word: Marshall would ride separately. As the bus reached its first stop in rural Newton, Marshall crept aboard — and was spotted by reporters doing so. He then joined the other candidates exiting to greet the crowd like he'd been there the whole time. Marshall is playing catch-up as he races to avoid becoming the first person to lose a Senate contest to a Democrat in the state in nearly a century. He faces the most serious challenger for a Kansas senator in over a decade as his party stares down a grim environment under President Donald Trump's second term. National Republicans are pouring millions into the state to prop him up; national Democrats are responding in kind, and Democrat Adam Hamilton, a well-known United Methodist pastor, is suddenly flush with cash for the campaign’s homestretch. But some Republicans think it’s already too late for Marshall. “He took it way too much for granted,” said former Kansas Gov. Mike Hayden, a Republican who supported Marshall’s previous campaigns but is now publicly backing Hamilton. “He's been almost invisible, except on national television. And there's not a lot of love in Kansas for Washington D.C.” National Republicans have privately urged Marshall to take his race more seriously on numerous occasions, according to a person familiar with the conversations who was granted anonymity to discuss them. Marshall, this person said, never appeared too worried about the race. Marshall’s latest Federal Election Commission report indicates this may be true. He raised just $866,000 for the third quarter to $9.9 million for Hamilton, and that filing did not appear to include any full-time payments to campaign staff. Marshall’s team did not respond to requests for comment on this article. One Republican strategist close to the White House, granted anonymity to speak candidly, acknowledged the race is an “uphill battle,” comparing Marshall to an “old athlete who, it takes them a lot longer to warm up to get ready for the game time, and they didn't start that early enough.” That strategist said that the remaining undecided voters are overwhelmingly Trump voters, and predicted they’d come home. Kansans “are mad at Republicans, but they just hate Democrats more,” the strategist said. “As much as DC Republicans are bedwetting, the ones actually working on the races are cognizant of this.” As the race nears the homestretch, a deluge of bad press has dogged the senator: His campaign used pictures of a Kansas campground without permission and had to edit the ad; his team faces accusations of blurring the line between his official and campaign offices; his campaign reportedly didn’t pay a bill to a local bakery for six years until after the unpaid debt was made public ( he apologized ). Two other stories landed the hardest. The first focuses on a Florida property that he owns, raising questions about how much time he actually spends in Kansas. The second stems from a New York Times report that Marshall, an obstetrician-gynecologist who served two terms in the U.S. House, had allegedly taken legal action against hundreds of medical patients who didn’t pay their bills. Marshall has said he spends the bulk of his time in Washington or Kansas, calling the claims “bologna.” He called the Times’ report a “hit job by left media” and told Fox News he had “nothing else to do to with the process” after patients’ accounts went to collections. At a Monday rally in the liberal college town of Lawrence, Hamilton told supporters that Kansans deserve a senator who isn’t just “showing up for photo ops” between “time with your family in Florida.” "I want to know from Roger Marshall: What's your plan when people … show up and they don't have health insurance?” Hamilton said, standing on a hay bale in a shady park. “Is the plan we're going to sue them? Then we're going to have some of them arrested, and maybe a few of them put in jail?" Hamilton’s campaign cut a face-to-camera ad with one of Marshall’s former patients, who said she was arrested when she was eight months pregnant because she missed a $50 payment to Marshall’s office. The Marshall campaign sent a cease-and-desist letter in response, saying the ad’s “message is false in every material respect,” and went up this week with its own ad of a former patient singing his praises. National Republicans have swooped in to prop up Marshall with $11 million in planned spending in recent days. And he’s getting other reinforcements: Chris Grant, the stalwart Trump-world operative and veteran of previous Marshall campaigns, will take an expanded role on the senator’s team through Election Day, Axios first reported . Marshall’s struggles are drawing unfavorable comparisons to the last Republican who needed to be bailed out to win a Senate race in the state. “This race reminds me of Sen. Pat Roberts’ last race [in 2014], when he was accused of not maintaining a Kansas residence and campaigning poorly,” said one Kansas state GOP lawmaker, who was granted anonymity to speak openly. But Republicans had a strong wind at their backs in 2014, sweeping nearly every Senate race that year; Roberts managed a 10-point win, similar to Marshall’s 11-point win in 2020. This time around, the national climate is blowing hard the other direction. Kansas has been especially hard-hit by some of Trump’s policies. His tariffs and spiking fuel prices left the state’s row crop farmers struggling. A plan to import cheap foreign beef infuriated ranchers in a state that produces the second-most cattle annually. And his threats to cut off U.S. sales of Bombardier planes — a Canadian company whose U.S. headquarters are in Wichita — rattled the state’s robust aviation industry. Marshall has recently shown signs he knows he’s in a fight. The normally strident MAGA backer broke with the president on the beef import plan and on a recent local immigration enforcement action, after ICE activity rattled some of his state’s agricultural towns. He’s banking on the conservative nature of the state, working hard to paint Hamilton as a progressive who will fall in line behind Washington Democrats. “This guy is the most radical liberal Democrat in the history of Kansas to get through a primary,” Marshall said in an interview in Garden City. “He is this wolf in sheep's clothing.” At rallies in Newton, Hutchinson, Dodge City and Garden City, he warned that his election could decide which party controls the upper chamber. “If my opponent were elected, it would give Chuck Schumer and AOC control of the Senate,” he repeated. Recent Republican ads hit Hamilton as “woke” and “radical,” pointing to his past praise of the Black Lives Matter movement. But as Marshall tagged along with the other GOP candidates for their barnstorming tour, holding mini-rallies across central and western Kansas on Tuesday, he was reminded how deep the anger at Washington runs right now — even in ruby-red Kansas. In Dodge City, the self-described “cattle capital” of the country, some Republicans in the crowd grumbled about spiking fuel prices. In Newton, protesters screamed through Marshall’s speech, calling Republicans “fascists.” (“Quiet, Satan!” a disgruntled attendee retorted.) In Garden City, where ICE activity sent shockwaves last month, Marshall got an earful in a private meeting with local lawmakers over their frustration that immigration officers barged into town without coordinating with local law enforcement. ”I think the frustration is still there,” state Rep. Jason Goetz, a Republican who represents some of the cities affected by ICE enforcement. There’s a belief among some Kansas Republicans that Marshall has thrown together so poor a campaign that if he wins, it won’t be of his own accord — it will be because of Ty Masterson, the Republican state Senate president running for governor who joined him on the bus tour and has polled a few points ahead of Marshall in most surveys. Rep. Tim Huelskamp, a Kansas Republican who lost a U.S. House primary to Marshall in 2016, said Masterson is “going to pull everybody across the line,” a list that “absolutely” includes Marshall. Patricia Woods, a Hutchinson resident, said at a rally that she is “100% behind Masterson.” When asked about Marshall, she said she is “kind of on the fence.” Masterson, when asked about Marshall’s race, simply chuckled. “It's more complicated than mine,” he said. Adam Wren and Andrew Howard contributed reporting.

articles.body: <p>Ocurrió ya en las generales de 2023, cuando Podemos hizo una <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2023-06-08/podemos-lanza-una-consulta-para-tener-plenos-poderes-sobre-la-decision-final-de-un-acuerdo-con-sumar.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2023-06-08/podemos-lanza-una-consulta-para-tener-plenos-poderes-sobre-la-decision-final-de-un-acuerdo-con-sumar.html">consulta a sus simpatizantes a 24 horas </a>de que venciera el plazo para el registro de coaliciones, y ha vuelto a pasar ahora. La izquierda alternativa, con siglas que varían en cada territorio, lleva una vez más al límite las negociaciones para alcanzar un acuerdo y presentarse en una lista única el 29-N. El principal escollo está en Madrid con el encaje en el Frente Amplio (la alianza que aúna a Comuns, IU, Más Madrid y Movimiento Sumar) de Irene Montero, que es la candidata con la que Podemos irrumpió antes que el resto de las fuerzas políticas en la arena preelectoral. El pulso se da también con otras organizaciones de carácter autonómico en cada comunidad, pero los pactos sí han avanzado este jueves en Aragón y Baleares (con acuerdo sin Podemos de momento con CHA y Més) o Canarias (este último cerrado ya con el partido de Ione Belarra, Nueva Canaria e IU bajo la marca “Unidad del pueblo canario”). En la Comunidad Valenciana, las conversaciones se han complicado en las últimas horas y Compromís podría acabar en una lista solo con Podemos. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-16/la-izquierda-alternativa-lleva-al-limite-el-pulso-para-las-listas-del-29-n-con-el-escollo-principal-de-madrid.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-14/el-psoe-aumenta-la-distancia-sobre-el-pp-hasta-los-118-puntos-tras-la-convocatoria-electoral-segun-el-cis.html" target="_self" rel="" El previsible resultado a favor de los votos de todos los partidos menos los de Vox y la abstención de Junts no ocultó que los discursos emitidos fueron ya de clara precampaña electoral. Al retrato tétrico de España pintado por los portavoces del PP y Vox, en el que repasaron casi uno por uno todos los escándalos y crisis padecidas en esta legislatura por el Gabinete de Pedro Sánchez, se sumó incluso con más ardor en esos ataques el portavoz de Junts, Josep Maria Cruset, lo que provocó la ira del representante de ERC, Gabriel <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-16/ultima-hora-de-la-actualidad-politica-en-directo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-16/ultima-hora-de-la-actualidad-politica-en-directo.html">Rufián, muy afectado por su reconocido fracaso en su pretensión de unir a toda la izquierda</a> para la cita con las urnas del 29-N.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-16/junts-se-alinea-con-el-discurso-mas-duro-de-pp-y-vox-en-uno-de-los-ultimos-debates-del-congreso.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El líder del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha insistido en reclamar al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, una respuesta “serena y firme” a Marruecos <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-12/buques-de-guerra-marroquies-invadieron-aguas-de-ceuta-coincidiendo-con-la-entrada-masiva-de-inmigrantes.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-12/buques-de-guerra-marroquies-invadieron-aguas-de-ceuta-coincidiendo-con-la-entrada-masiva-de-inmigrantes.html">por la incursión de sus buques en aguas españolas</a> coincidiendo con la entrada masiva de inmigrantes de finales de julio, como desveló EL PAÍS. “Los continuos desafíos a la soberanía nacional no pueden ocultarse. Una nación que aspira a ser respetada debe empezar haciéndose respetar”, ha reclamado Feijóo en un acto con mujeres del mundo rural este viernes en Toledo. articles.body: <p>El juez de la Audiencia Nacional Antonio Piña ha acordado dar carpetazo a las diligencias que abrió el pasado abril a raíz de la denuncia presentada por el partido extraparlamentario Iustitia Europa contra el primer ministro de Israel, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-04-17/la-audiencia-nacional-pregunta-a-la-fiscalia-si-puede-investigar-a-netanyahu-por-la-detencion-de-un-casco-azul-espanol-en-el-libano.html" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-04-17/la-audiencia-nacional-pregunta-a-la-fiscalia-si-puede-investigar-a-netanyahu-por-la-detencion-de-un-casco-azul-espanol-en-el-libano.html">Benjamín Netanyahu</a>, por la presunta <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-04-08/el-ejercito-israeli-detiene-durante-casi-una-hora-a-un-soldado-espanol-en-libano.html#:~:text=Un%20casco%20azul%20espa%C3%B1ol%20fue%20detenido%20este,el%20embajador%20liban%C3%A9s%20en%20Madrid%2C%20Hani%20Chemaitelly." rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-04-08/el-ejercito-israeli-detiene-durante-casi-una-hora-a-un-soldado-espanol-en-libano.html#:~:text=Un%20casco%20azul%20espa%C3%B1ol%20fue%20detenido%20este,el%20embajador%20liban%C3%A9s%20en%20Madrid%2C%20Hani%20Chemaitelly.">detención ilegal de un casco azul español</a> que formaba parte de la misión de la ONU en el Líbano. En una resolución, a la que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS, el instructor explica que adopta esta decisión porque constan “investigaciones actualmente en curso, tanto en el ámbito institucional de Naciones Unidas como ante las autoridades del Estado de Israel”. articles.body: El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha elevat els avisos per pluja a Barcelona , un episodi que arriba quan encara són presents els efectes del darrer temporal, de principis d’octubre. En previsió de forts aiguats, aquest dissabte, hi ha set comarques en avís vermell , entre les quals hi ha el Barcelonès, i 10 més en avís taronja. De moment, els aiguats han descarregat amb força al Vallès Oriental i al Maresme , on els Bombers busquen una dona desapareguda després de caure a la riera de Cabrera de Mar. A Barcelona, els xàfecs van per barris. Tot i això una potent tempesta ha aturat temporalment l’operativa a l’aeroport del Prat i ha provocat múltiples retards i cancel·lacions. Davant la previsió meteorològica adversa, Protecció Civil té activada l’ alerta del pla Inuncat i ha enviat un missatge ES-Alert a les comarques que estan en avís vermell amb recomanacions per reduir la mobilitat. En aquesta pàgina pots seguir minut a minut l’ última hora d’aquesta alerta per pluges intenses a Barcelona i Catalunya i totes les afectacions.  També et pot interessar Avís vermell per pluja intensa a Barcelona: Protecció Civil envia un ES-Alert amb recomanacions Marta Casals Torres Sílvia Gutiérrez 3 minuts de lectura

articles.body: Júlia Serrat és un dels noms del moment a l’Europa . És la propietària del carril esquerre i titular indiscutible en un club on va aterrar fa tres anys. Després d’un estiu de canvis al vestidor, va decidir quedar-se al Nou Sardenya . “Fa només tres anys que jugo aquí però és casa meva. Som una família, no puc demanar més”, diu la lateral. La cama esquerra de Júlia Serrat no només regala màgia als camps de futbol 11. La jugadora manresana també forma part de la selecció espanyola de futbol platja . Campiona del mundialet fa quatre dies amb Espanya i campiona d’Europa fa un mes. En la final contra el Brasil va contribuir amb un gol en la final disputada al Puerto de Santa Maria. Al betevé esports parlem amb Serrat de la dualitat dels dos esports. També et pot interessar betevé emetrà en directe l’Europa – Deportivo de la Corunya de la Copa de la Reina Pablo Agudo 1 minut de lectura La protagonista de l’eliminatòria de Copa contra el Vila-real Júlia Serrat va ser la gran artífex amb dos grans gols del triomf contra el Vila-real per 4-0 en la segona ronda de la Copa de la Reina . “Feia molt que no jugàvem Copa al Nou Sardenya i teníem ganes. Els gols els vaig celebrar molt, el segon recordo tirar-me al terra i mirar la grada. Fer-li quatre gols a tot un Vila-real i mantenir la porteria a zero s’ha de valorar molt”, diu la jugadora escapulada. El pròxim repte a la Copa de la Reina serà superar un equip de la Lliga F per accedir als vuitens de final: al Deportivo de la Corunya . Un partit que es disputarà el dijous 5 de novembre i que es podrà seguir en directe a betevé.

articles.body: Aquest dissbabte 17 d’octubre fa 40 anys d’aquell moment que molts barcelonins tenen en la memòria com una de les frases que van canviar la història i, sobretot, la ciutat de Barcelona. A Lausana, a Suïssa, Joan Antoni Samaranch va obrir un sobre que revelava quina seria la pròxima ciutat a acollir uns jocs olímpics: Barcelona. I ho va dir amb una pausa dramàtica que va posar a prova els nervis d’un país. À la ville de Barcelona “Le Comité International Olympique, réuni en session plénière à Lausanne, a attribué l’organisation de jeu de la 25e Olympiade 1992 à la ville de… Attendez un moment… À la ville de… Barcelona” Joan Antoni Samaranch (17 d’octubre del 1986, Lausana, Suïssa) Aquella frase dona títol al documental que Visiona TV ha fet per a betevé i que s’estrena dissabte, a les 21.30 h, al programa Punt de fuga . També et pot interessar Hospital de Sant Pau: sis segles d’història i un de modernisme, en un reportatge del ‘Punt de fuga’ Laura Sangrà Herrero 3 minuts de lectura Els qui ho recorden El treball reuneix alguns personatges que van quedar marcats per aquell moment: Queco Novell, Sílvia Cóppulo, Jordi Amat, Quim Masferrer, Los Manolos (Rogeli Herrero i Xavier Calero), Elisabeth Maragall i Judit Mascó. La nominació olímpica va influir en les seves trajectòries personals i professionals i el seu testimoni ens ajuda a fer-ne memòria. Els qui hi eren El documental dona veu també als protagonistes del moment, com l’exministre de Defensa, exalcalde de Barcelona i primer impulsor del projecte olímpic, Narcís Serra , el fill de Joan Antoni Samaranch i dos dels fills de Leopoldo Rodés.

articles.body: El Barça volia allargar la ratxa imparable de victòries i ha sortit a La Cartuja amb les idees ben clares, tot i que amb alguns canvis en l’onze inicial, amb Jules Kounde, Xavi Espart i Karim Adeyemi . Una primera part boja, molt entretinguda per a l’espectador, ha donat avantatge mínim al Barça (1-2) i a la represa els blaugrana han reblat el clau amb tres gols més, tot i que el Betis ha acabat amb un home menys sobre el terreny de joc (2-5) . Els gols blaugrana han anat a càrrec de Lamine Yamal, Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric i Dani Olmo. Per part del Betis, han marcat Valentín Gómez i Ez Abde . Dos a cinc a La Cartuja i nou victòries en nou partits de Lliga. Deliri de primera part amb victòria parcial del Barça El Barça ha deixat passar només 10 minuts per marcar. I ha estat per insistència: ha buscat el gol des de l’inici i en un intercanvi arrencant des del mig del camp Kounde ha assistit Lamine Yamal, que s’ha tret de la màniga una genialitat , s’ha col·locat la pilota cap a dins i ha connectat una rosca espectacular que ha tret les teranyines de la porteria de Valles . En una jugada a pilota aturada des del córner, ha arribat l’empat del Betis . Ningú ha allunyat el perill del córner, Fornals ha recollit l’esfèrica, ha centrat i l’ argentí Valentín Gómez de cap ha superat Joan Garcia . Adeyemi ha tingut l’1 a 2 a tocar , amb una assistència precisa de Lamine Yamal, però ha topat amb el porter bètic, Álvaro Valles, que ha tret la pilota quan el tenia al davant. I Joan Garcia, ben col·locat sota pals, ha mantingut els reflexos per desviar el gran xut d’Héctor Bellerín . I del possible 2 a 1, sense temps per respirar, el córner que ha servit Fermín, Rodrigo Hernández ha guanyat la posició i l’ha rematat de cap, i ha aconseguit així l’1 a 2 i el seu primer gol com a blaugrana . Lo Celso ha aconseguit un golàs , engaltant la pilota, mitja volta perfecta i volea que ha significat el 2 a 2. Però ben bé a l’ inici de la jugada, Cucho s’ha emportat la pilota amb el braç i, per tant, després de la revisió pertinent del VAR , l’àrbitre De Burgos Bengoechea ha anul·lat el gol sota fortes protestes del públic de La Cartuja i la banqueta bètica, amb un Pellegrini desbocat. Nit de bogeria, gols a dojo i expulsió de Bernal, del Betis La segona meitat ha començat elèctrica. Primer s’ha anul·lat un gol al Barça per fora de joc de Gabriel Jesus, que havia rebut una altra assistència de luxe de Lamine Yamal . En la jugada següent, els mateixos protagonistes, Lamine i Gabriel Jesus , aquesta vegada sí que han culminat el gol, assistència del primer i seguretat de Jesus per finalitzar amb una definició impecable . L’acció ha seguit: només un minut després, el Betis ha retallat distàncies i Abde en un u contra u amb el porter blaugrana, Joan Garcia , no ha perdonat. Després del segon gol del conjunt andalús hi ha hagut una picabaralla sobre la gespa. Fermín reclamava una falta i les queixes a l’àrbitre han acabat amb Lamine per terra per un cop de cap d’un jugador del Betis, Facundo Bernal . Bernal, per culpa d’aquesta agressió sense pilota, ha resultat expulsat per De Burgos Bengoechea. El Barça ha seguit pressionant i ha obtingut el premi del quart gol en un llançament de falta . Lamine Yamal ha penjat la pilota , que ha rebotat en la barrera dels jugadors del Betis, i l’ha recollit Cubarsí, que, tot i xocar amb el porter Valles, ha assistit cap enrere cap a Eric, que ha xutat dins . El cinquè ha arribat en el 82, quan Dani Olmo ha rebut una passada mil·limètrica de Cubarsí, el de Terrassa ha conduït i ha aconseguit marcar . articles.body: La previsió del temps per a aquest diumenge, 18 d’octubre, continua marcada per la inestabilitat , amb pluja i un ambient de plena tardor . És recomanable mantenir el paraigua i la màniga llarga ben a prop . La pluja caurà de forma minsa i continuada gran part del dia. Previsió horària per a Barcelona : 6 h: ruixats moderats 9 h: cel ben tapat, amb plugims 12 h: ambient de tardor, amb valors per sota dels 17 ºC 15 h: gregal intens a la façana marítima 18 h: una altra tongada de ruixats 21 h: nit de ruixats i fresca d’uns 12 ºC També et pot interessar Avís vermell per pluja intensa a Barcelona: Protecció Civil envia un ES-Alert amb recomanacions Marta Casals Torres Sílvia Gutiérrez 3 minuts de lectura Pluja menys intensa però força continuada Després dels aiguats de la nit i matinada, sembla que arribarà el gregal , un vent que no porta tanta pluja a Barcelona. De fet, la dita ja diu que “El gregal la mou i el llevant la plou” , tot i que aquest diumenge tindrem una mica de tot. El dia serà ben rúfol , amb cel gris i plugims que aniran caient al llarg del dia. Sembla que podrien tenir més entitat fins a mig matí i tornar a aparèixer a darrera hora del dia. També hi ha haurà moments de treva , però l’ambient humit seguirà sent protagonista. Pel que fa a les temperatures, tindrem un dia de plena tardor , com si fóssim al novembre. L’ambient humit i el cel tapat faran que l’amplitud tèrmica entre les mínimes i les màximes sigui ben poc destacable. Les mínimes es donaran a darrera hora del dia , amb valors que quedaran per sota dels 15 ºC . Les màximes no pujaran més enllà i les més altes quedaran al voltant dels 16 o 17 ºC . La inestabilitat té corda per a uns quants dies La dana Adam , situada a l’oest peninsular, ens enviarà vents humits de mar cap a terra durant unes jornades més. Diumenge sembla que el gregal incidirà de ple cap al País Valencià i el sud de les Balears i afectarà punts del Camp de Tarragona fins a mitja tarda. El vent del nord-est intens portarà una mar moguda i molts núvols i fresca arreu. Tot i que la incertesa és ben elevada, sembla que dilluns els vents de llevant podrien tornar a afectar de ple Catalunya i portar-nos més pluges que podrien ser generals i abundants fins dimarts . Tot i així, caldrà seguir de ben a prop els propers moviments dels mapes. A mitjans de setmana, el temps millorarà de manera clara , però es mantindrà un ambient força propi de la tardor , sobretot durant les hores nocturnes. articles.body: L’expectativa per veure en acció Bisiwu i Hamza Abdelkarim amb el Barça Atlètic no ha decebut, si més no a l’inici de l’enfrontament contra l’Utebo. La primera pilota que ha arribat a l’extrem belga ha acabat amb penal favorable als blaugrana després d’una conducció i un parell de retalls. Hamza ha agafat la responsabilitat i no ha fallat . Minut 6 i 1 a 0 en, també, la primera pilota que ha tocat. L’efervescència i les ganes de veure en acció els dos titulars s’ha diluït, com el joc. La resta de la primera meitat ha estat ensopida, sense res destacable per part dels dos equips, més enllà d’una arribada dels aragonesos després d’un regal de Hafiz. Pedro Rodríguez sentencia a la represa Barrero ha avisat a la segona, però Iker Rodríguez l’ha enviat a córner. La resposta, gairebé immediata, ha anat a càrrec de Catovic amb un obús que ha obligat Nono a estirar-se. Bisiwu , amb una centrada xut, ha tingut a tocar el segon abans de deixar el camp. El temps s’anava dilatant pels espectadors del Johan davant la manca d’ocasions, fins que Pedro Rodríguez ha fet el segon amb un xut des de la frontal al minut 72 i ha despertat a tothom a la graderia. Semblava que el marcador ja no es mouria més, però el 2 a 1 de Lybomirov ha fet que els 799 espectadors del Johan Cruyff patissin als quatre minuts de descompte. articles.body: TMB ha instal·lat barreres antiinundacions en un dels accessos de l’estació de Parc Logístic, de l’L9S, davant la previsió de pluges torrencials per a aquest vespre a Barcelona . Aquestes tanques són unes estructures de plàstic en forma de ela que permeten desviar l’aigua i evitar així inundacions a les instal·lacions i equipaments de l’estació. Es tracta d’una prova pilot i s’ha escollit la parada de Parc Logístic perquè va ser una de les més afectades per les inundacions causades per les tempestes de principis d’octubre . Joan Granés, responsable de manteniment d’infraestructures, estacions i túnels de metro de Barcelona, explica que TMB ha iniciat els tràmits per comprar barreres d’aquest tipus , que s’utilitzarien a diferents estacions en casos d’episodis de pluges torrencials. “Estem mirant diferents proveïdors que ens el puguin subministrar, avui fem la prova pilot i en funció de l’èxit que tingui aquesta prova farem una compra més endavant de més material”. També et pot interessar Avís vermell per pluja intensa a Barcelona: Protecció Civil envia un ES-Alert amb recomanacions Marta Casals Torres Sílvia Gutiérrez 3 minuts de lectura Fàcils de posar i treure Les barreres que s’han instal·lat al metro han estat cedides pels Bombers de Barcelona , que són també els qui les han col·locat en aquesta primera prova al metro. Són les mateixes tanques que es van col·locar amb èxit a l’escola i l’institut Bosc de Montjuïc i que van evitar inundacions posteriors a tot dos centres. Aquestes estructures són d’instal·lació fàcil i ràpida i permeten d’una manera efectiva desviar l’aigua per protegir els diferents equipaments. “Són molt fàcils de posar, i molt fàcils de treure i aquesta és la virtut”, explica el cap d’unitat de Bombers de Barcelona, Carlos Chico Tapias, ” actuen de manera molt ràpida, quan més forta està l’aigua, més fort s’arrela al paviment”. També et pot interessar Tanques provisionals a l’escola i l’institut Bosc de Montjuïc, un nou aliat contra les inundacions Marta de San Nicolás 2 minuts de lectura Ús de sacs de sorra De moment, TMB ha iniciat els tràmits per comprar barreres d’aquest tipus per utilitzar-les a diferents estacions en casos d’episodis de pluges torrencials. Mentre no es disposi d’aquestes estructures, TMB ha previst altres maneres de protegir els accessos a les estacions, com ara l’ús de sacs de sorra per contenir l’entrada d’aigua.

articles.body: El Congrés de Clubs 2026 ha posat el punt final aquest dissabte al Reial Club de Polo de Barcelona després de reunir més de 450 representants de clubs i federacions esportius catalans en una edició que ha exhaurit totes les places disponibles. La trobada, impulsada per la UFEC i el Departament d’Esports de la Generalitat , ha comptat amb 40 ponents , que han compartit experiències i eines en àmbits com el lideratge, la sostenibilitat financera, la innovació, la intel·ligència artificial, l’impacte social i la gestió d’instal·lacions esportives. Dues jornades d’activitat intensa La jornada de clausura ha comptat amb la participació del conseller d’Esports, Berni Álvarez; el regidor d’Esports de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona, David Escudé, i el president de la UFEC, Gerard Esteva . Tots tres han coincidit a destacar la necessitat que clubs, federacions i institucions treballin de manera coordinada per afrontar els reptes de futur del sector. Sota el lema “De la gestió diària al lideratge d’alt rendiment”, el congrés s’ha consolidat com un espai de referència per al debat i la formació, amb l’objectiu d’ enfortir el paper dels clubs esportius com a motor esportiu i social de Catalunya . Durant les dues jornades s’han organitzat ponències, debats i casos pràctics centrats en la gestió dels clubs esportius. Entre els temes destacats hi ha hagut el lideratge i el bon govern, la sostenibilitat financera, la relació entre empresa i esport, la innovació tecnològica i l’impacte social de les entitats. També s’han abordat els reptes de futur de les instal·lacions esportives municipals, en una edició que ha volgut oferir eines i recursos perquè els clubs puguin adaptar-se a un entorn cada vegada més exigent i professionalitzat.
articles.headline: El Congrés de Clubs tanca amb èxit i reforça l’aposta pel lideratge i la professionalització

articles.body: L’Espanyol ha encaixat una derrota cruel davant l’Atlètic de Madrid , que s’endú els tres punts de Cornellà gràcies a una obra d’art d’Álex Baena a les acaballes del partit. Els blanc-i-blaus només han sumat un punt dels últims 12 . L’equip de Manolo González ha sortit espès al terreny de joc, amb un rival que ha tingut la iniciativa des dels primers compassos. Els matalassers han tingut les primeres internades, impulsats per un Kang-In Lee molt participatiu. Una acció de talent del sud-coreà ha deixat un mà a mà a Giuliano Simeone , però l’argentí no ha estat precís en el moment de la rematada. Entre Hinojo i Riedel han refusat la pilota a córner . Intercanvi de cops a partir de la mitja hora de joc Un cop superat l’equador de la primera meitat, han arribat les ocasions més clares del primer temps. L’Espanyol ha tret el cap amb una doble oportunitat. Javi Hernández i Roberto , en accions consecutives, no han pogut avançar els seus. L’última de la primera meitat també ha estat de color blanc-i-blau. Gairebé a tocar del descans, Lele Cabrera ha rematat amb la cama dreta una segona jugada des de la frontal, en una pilota que s’ha acabat estavellant al travesser i que no ha aconseguit desfer l’empat a zero. Cholo Simeone ha aprofitat el temps de descans per moure les peces i introduir els primers canvis: primer, Julián Álvarez i Alejandro Grimaldo i als 10 minuts de la segona part, Marcos Llorente . Precisament el 14 dels madrilenys ha tingut a les botes una gran oportunitat per obrir la llauna, en una pilota que ha caçat alliberat a la frontal de l’àrea i que ha acabat enviant al travesser . Ho ha seguit intentant l’equip del Cholo, però sense encert. En aquest cas, Fortuño ha hagut de fer una doble aturada, primer, a Jonathan David i després, a Julián , que continua sense veure porteria aquesta temporada. L’Espanyol ha començat a acusar el cansament . També et pot interessar Del Sants a Primera: Alex Calatrava, el seu pas pel futbol català i el canvi Europa – Sant Andreu Pablo Agudo 2 minuts de lectura El retorn de Puado després de nou mesos Una de les notícies més positives de la tarda ha estat l’entrada de Javi Puado . El capità blanc-i-blau ha disputat els últims 10 minuts de partit en la seva reaparició després d’un llarg període d’inactivitat, a causa de la lesió que es va fer l’11 de gener davant el Llevant . Quan semblava que tots dos equips marxarien amb un punt a la butxaca, ha aparegut el talent dels visitants . Julián Álvarez , amb una acció des de la banda esquerra, ha eliminat dos rivals i ha deixat Álex Baena sol a la frontal. L’andalús ha enviat la pilota a l’escaire i ha fet impossible l’estirada de Fortuño . La derrota deixa tocat un Espanyol que no guanya des del 12 de setembre . Provisionalment, els de Manolo són dotzens amb vuit punts en nou jornades. La propera oportunitat per buscar tornar al camí de la victòria serà el dissabte 24 al camp del Racing de Santander .
articles.headline: Un golàs de Baena condemna l’Espanyol davant l’Atlètic de Madrid en el retorn de Javi Puado
